newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia army creates pipeline protection force.
newsitem.headline: Colombia army creates pipeline protection force.

text.p: A new army brigade has been set up in eastern Colombia to defend strategic oil infrastructure from leftist rebel dynamite attacks, army commander Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett said on Thursday.
The 18th brigade, comprising more than 4,000 men, includes four counter-insurgency battallions.
It will be based in oil-rich Arauca province, the centre for U.S. multinational Occidental Petroleum's operations and the starting point for the country's biggest oil pipeline.

"The creation of this brigade will increase our capacity to protect the oil infrastructure in the department and protect the lives of military engineers many of whom have been killed by guerrillas," Bonett said.

The National Liberation Army (ELN), the country's second largest guerrilla force, has bombed the pipeline which starts at Cano Limon and runs to the Caribbean coast oil terminal of Covenas more than 40 times this year alone. State-run oil company Ecopetrol said damage and lost production had cost more than $38 million.
